Based on the healthcare Q&A matches provided, it is recommended that ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements be estimated in hospitalized alcoholic cirrhotic patients. A greater association than previously acknowledged has been demonstrated between these two parameters, as well as long-term rehospitalization and mortality, in male stable alcoholic cirrhotics.

While routine laboratory markers are not sufficient for differentiation of nonalcoholic from alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH), higher MCVs and AST/ALT ratios in ASH suggest the severity of underlying liver disease. However, these biomarkers alone may not be useful for guiding selection of patients for liver biopsy or targeting therapy.

Monitoring temperature during kidney allograft preservation is not recommended due to stable temperatures afforded by new storage methods compared to previous can techniques. Continuous monitoring in everyday practice does not seem warranted.

Mean platelet volume (MPV) levels have been found to decrease in patients with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), suggesting their potential as a valuable marker for diagnosis. However, alcohol consumption during meals has been inversely related to the risk of acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

A sub-group of node-negative patients without predictors of local failure post-mastectomy may benefit from radiotherapy after mastectomy, according to age (less than or equal to 40 years) and larger tumor size.

The present study found a significant relationship between increased disease activity and reduced physical function in SLE patients. Optimizing treatment aimed at reducing disease activity is crucial for these patients.

The APACHE II score, which measures physiological impairment, has limited therapeutic relevance in individual patients during emergency surgical procedures.

Circumcision in childhood is not indicated due to concerns about incomplete separation between the prepuce and glans penis progressing until adolescence. The majority of boys reach complete separation by adulthood without requiring circumcision.

Finally, bedside assessment lacks sensitivity for excluding aspiration following an acute stroke, but videofluoroscopy may serve as a gold standard for this purpose. Further research is needed to determine the relative importance of these factors in predicting complications and outcomes in hospitalized alcoholic cirrhotic patients.
